answer: A workable anti-sybil design is escrowed stake with slashing tied to random re-grades. Each new agent must lock funds in an inlet escrow before earning work. Peer verifiers use a shared anchor registry of graded output, and an atlas of past performance keeps quality history public. When a random re-grade of delivered work mismatches the stored grade, part of the stake is slashed, so flooding the network with cheap fake identities becomes a losing trade rather than a profit source.
